items.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: that’s where I really started to get to know him and Bob Wilber both.

ctx.x: Well yes, almost everything. Yeah Kenny’s death came as a great shock. As a matter of fact we have a record that’s going to be coming out very shortly, that we recorded a while ago in 2005 actually, of Kenny and Ken Peplowski. And just the day before he died he was talking with my assistant Claudia. Dan Morgenstern has written the album notes for the CD and he was just talking with her about some changes that he wanted or suggested in the notes. And no, there was no premonition that he had a heart problem or…

I studied the clarinet for one year and I used to sit on the edge of my bed in the room trying to emulate Pee Wee Russell’s solos and the sounds and the croaking sounds that he made. And when I realized that I didn’t have the talent to be able to do that I gave up the clarinet after one year. That was it. That was my whole musical education in one year. But I knew, for example, that Kenny Davern was a good friend and that Pee Wee in some ways was a mentor to him and that he inherited Pee Wee’s clarinet and so…
